passage:
I'm Om, and I sit two benches behind Tarun in Class 10. Last term he and Hemant did everything together: same auto, same bench, same terrible jokes. Then Tarun got tagged in photos of Ryan's group, the ones with the matching jackets. Within two weeks he was sitting with them at lunch, wearing the jacket, laughing a little late at things.

Hemant kept saving a seat at the old bench. Tarun walked past it, looking at his phone. I can't say if he felt bad. Once I saw him glance back at Hemant's bag on the empty seat, then delete something from his phone.

qa.q: What did Tarun start wearing?
qa.a: Tarun started wearing the matching jacket.

qa.q: What might Tarun have felt glancing back at Hemant's bag on the empty seat?
qa.a: Tarun may have felt a private ache or guilt, though Om cannot be certain.

qa.q: What could Tarun do next if the ache is real?
qa.a: Tarun could talk to Hemant and say the seat mattered, instead of walking past looking at the phone.

qa.q: What might it be like for Hemant, saving a seat that stays empty?
qa.a: Hemant probably felt hurt and confused, still hoping Tarun would come back and left waiting each day.

grounding: A teenager climbs the status ladder, leaves behind someone they did everything with and feels a private ache, as seen by a student two benches behind.

passage:
Monday. Sunaina's phone buzzed: the popular group had tagged her in a photo. Twelve likes in ten minutes. She stared at it, smiling.

Thursday. At lunch Sharmila waved from their old table by the window. Sunaina looked at the group's table, then at her plate. “Tomorrow,” she mouthed, and sat with the others. Someone said, “Isn't that your friend with the weird lunchbox?” Sunaina laughed.

The following Tuesday Sunaina saw Sharmila sitting alone, folding a paper bag into smaller and smaller squares. Something twisted inside her. She turned her phone face-down and kept looking at the group's table anyway.

qa.q: How many likes did the tagged photo get in ten minutes?
qa.a: The tagged photo got twelve likes in ten minutes.

qa.q: What did Sunaina feel on the following Tuesday, seeing Sharmila alone?
qa.a: Sunaina felt a private twist of guilt and ache, though staying with the popular group still felt important.

qa.q: What choice did Sunaina make on Thursday at lunch?
qa.a: Sunaina mouthed “Tomorrow” to Sharmila and sat with the popular group instead.

qa.q: What might Sharmila be feeling while folding the paper bag into smaller squares?
qa.a: Sharmila probably feels hurt and lonely, trying to look busy while wondering why Sunaina stopped coming.

grounding: A teenager judges standing by who sits with them and who tags them, drops an old friend and feels a private ache.

passage:
Pranav, you're worried about who sits with you in the canteen? Let me tell you about your Ankita bua at fifteen.
In Class 10, I started counting things. Who waited for me after school. Who wrote on my birthday. How many people signed my slam book. The popular girls, Neeta's group, had started saving me a seat.
My oldest friend Shobha still wore her hair in two plaits and brought idlis in a steel box. Neeta's girls laughed at the idlis. So one day I just stopped sitting with Shobha. I didn't say anything. I simply walked past her table.
I climbed. By March, I was in all the photos.
But every time I saw Shobha eating alone, there was an ache. It's still there, a little, forty years later.

qa.q: What did Shobha bring for lunch?
qa.a: She brought idlis in a steel box.

qa.q: How did young Ankita feel seeing Shobha eat alone?
qa.a: She felt a private ache of guilt and sadness, even while enjoying her new status.

qa.q: At what point in the story could Ankita have made a different choice?
qa.a: When Neeta's girls laughed at the idlis, she could have kept sitting with Shobha, or invited her along.

qa.q: How might Shobha have felt when Ankita walked past her table?
qa.a: She likely felt hurt and abandoned, dropped by her oldest friend without a word.

grounding: An elder recalls, as a teen, measuring her status by seats and signatures and dropping an old friend, feeling a lasting private ache.

passage:
The farewell photographer had five minutes before the light went. “Groups, quickly!” he shouted.
Pankaj looked around. On one side, Baljeet, his friend since Class 1, was waving him over to stand with the chess club boys. On the other side, Karan's group, the cricket team, the ones everyone tagged, were shouting, “Pankaj! Here!”
He thought of the photo on everyone's profile tomorrow. Who would be tagged. Who would be seen.
He walked to Karan's group. Click.
Afterwards, he saw Baljeet folding up the chess club banner alone. Baljeet didn't look up.
That night the photo got two hundred likes. Pankaj looked at it for a long time, and then at an old photo of him and Baljeet, age seven, with ice-cream on their faces.

qa.q: How many likes did the photo get?
qa.a: It got two hundred likes.

qa.q: What was Pankaj feeling as he looked at the old photo?
qa.a: He felt a private ache and guilt, knowing he had left Baljeet to be seen with the popular group.

qa.q: What could Pankaj do to repair things with Baljeet?
qa.a: He could message Baljeet, say sorry for walking away, and ask for a photo together before school ends.

qa.q: How might Baljeet have felt folding the banner alone?
qa.a: Baljeet was probably hurt and let down, watching the oldest friend choose the popular group.

grounding: Shows a teenager under time pressure choosing to be photographed with the popular group over an old friend, then feeling a private ache.

passage:
Jagdish checked his phone again on the bus home in Pune. Eighteen likes on his new profile picture. He'd changed it twice because the first one got only nine.
At school, he'd started noticing everything. Who waited for him at the gate. Who tagged him. Whether Arjun's group made space at lunch. When they did, he felt taller all day.
Yamini, from his building, messaged: “Walking to tuition together today?” They'd walked together since Class 6. But Arjun's group thought Yamini was “too serious”, always in the library.
He typed, “Going early today, sorry,” and walked with Arjun's group instead.
Through the tuition window, he saw Yamini walking alone. He felt a small, sharp ache and looked back at his likes.

qa.q: How many likes did his first profile picture get?
qa.a: It got only nine.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling when he saw Yamini walking alone?
qa.a: He felt a small, sharp ache of guilt, knowing he'd dropped her to keep his status.

qa.q: What went wrong in how Jagdish chose his company?
qa.a: He let likes and the group's opinion decide, dropping a real friend; he could walk with Yamini and still be friends with Arjun's group.

qa.q: How might Yamini have felt after getting his message?
qa.a: Yamini was probably puzzled and a little hurt, walking alone after years of walking together.

grounding: Shows a teenager measuring his status by likes and seats, dropping an old friend who seems uncool and feeling a private ache.

passage:
"Zainab! Saved you a seat," Naveen called from their old corner of the canteen, two samosas on a plate.
Zainab slowed. At the middle table, Tanya was waving too. Tanya, whose posts got three hundred likes, who had tagged Zainab in a story for the first time last night.
"Actually, Tanya asked me to sit with them today," Zainab said.
"Oh." Naveen looked at the second samosa. "Tomorrow, then?"
"Yeah. Maybe."
At the middle table, Tanya said, "Wait, you used to sit with that quiz guy?"
"Not really," Zainab said quickly. "He just sat near me."
Everyone laughed. Zainab laughed too, and checked her reflection in her phone screen.
Across the canteen, Naveen was eating alone, the second samosa still on the plate. Zainab looked away first.

qa.q: What was on Naveen's plate?
qa.a: Two samosas.

qa.q: What does Zainab looking away first suggest?
qa.a: Zainab feels a private ache of guilt, knowing she dropped a loyal friend to gain standing with Tanya's table.

qa.q: What could Zainab do tomorrow to begin repairing things?
qa.a: Sit with Naveen, admit that saying "not really" was unfair, and stop treating friendships as rungs on a ladder.

qa.q: What is lunch like for Naveen?
qa.a: Naveen feels hurt and lonely, eating by himself with the samosa he saved still on the plate 😔

grounding: Shows a teenager judging standing by who tags and sits with her, dropping an old friend to climb and feeling a private ache about it.
